samples.summary: `latencyMeasured` is derived from array-ness, so an EMPTY or latency-less records array retires the declared gap while producing no number and no shortfall reason
samples.evidence: `coderabbitLatency` sets `requested: true` for any array (line 621: `if (!Array.isArray(perItem))`), and `declaredGaps({ latencyMeasured: latency.requested })` (line 866) then drops `coderabbit_latency_ms` entirely. With `latency: []` (or an array whose entries carry no `latency` object — `lats` is filtered by `.filter(Boolean)` at line 632), `n_items === 0` and `self_timed.n === 0`, so the completeness guard `latency.self_timed.n < latency.n_items` at line 797 is `0 < 0` → false: no reason is pushed, `verdict` can stay `complete`, and `renderReport` prints `declared gaps — none: every metric §3.4 asks for is either measured above or not asked of this scorer` (line 962) plus `latency [...]: n/a (n=0) — 0 of 0 item(s) poolable`. The state the whole block is designed to make impossible — a retired gap with no figure behind it — is reachable, and `requested` is not evidence that anything was measured. A predicate like `latency.self_timed.ms.n > 0` (or `n_items > 0`) is what the gap's own wording ("the read exists and this run was given it") implies.

samples.summary: The latency coverage denominator is the injected list, not the requested corpus, so items never timed at all are invisible rather than reported as a shortfall
samples.evidence: Line 797 compares `latency.self_timed.n` against `latency.n_items`, and `n_items` is `perItem.map(it => it?.latency).filter(Boolean).length` (line 632/652) — i.e. how many records happened to arrive. Every other coverage check in this function is against the REQUESTED corpus (`corpusIds.filter(id => !seen.has(id))`, line 767, which produces `N corpus item(s) never replayed`). So a latency read covering 3 of 7 corpus items reports `3 of 3 item(s) poolable` and `verdict: complete`; nothing cross-checks the latency records' `item_id`s against `corpusItemIds`, even though the CLI deliberately carries `item_id` through at line 1088. `corpusRecords` accepts an `itemId` filter (adapters/coderabbit.mjs:1136), so a single-item read injected by any other caller silently reads as full coverage.

samples.summary: Suppressing the push-proxy shortfall wholesale also suppresses genuine read failures (`check-runs-unavailable`), which can no longer reach the exit code
samples.evidence: The guard at 788–803 only ever inspects `self_timed`, justified by the on-demand exclusion being by design. But `push_proxy` also goes non-poolable for `check-runs-unavailable` (a failed `gh` read — adapters/coderabbit.mjs:937, degraded to `null` by `checkRunsFor`, coderabbit.mjs:1091) and for `no-check-run`. Those are our own read failures, described in the adapter as "OUR failure, and the fix is to re-run", yet with this guard a run where every check-runs call timed out prints `0 of 7 item(s) poolable` on the proxy and still exits 0 (`process.exitCode` at line 1100 follows `completeness.verdict`). Excluding only the by-design cause (`poolable === false` on an on-demand trigger, distinguishable via `census.push_proxy.absent`) would keep the design exclusion silent without swallowing a failed read.

samples.summary: The self_timed shortfall pools unfixable absences with re-runnable ones, so a corpus containing one clean CodeRabbit review exits 1 permanently
samples.evidence: `latency.self_timed.n < latency.n_items` pushes a completeness reason regardless of WHY the item has no figure. `LATENCY_ABSENT` (adapters/coderabbit.mjs:812) separates causes precisely because some are permanent facts, not shortfalls: `no-finding` ("CodeRabbit reviewed this pull request cleanly — a clean review is not a zero-length one") and `no-review-commit` can never be fixed by re-running, yet both force `verdict: "partial"` and `process.exitCode = 1` forever. That is the exact argument the adjacent comment (lines 791–794) uses to justify excluding the push proxy, applied inconsistently: the causes are available in `census.self_timed.absent` and could be partitioned into blocking vs reported.

samples.summary: A mis-shaped `coderabbit.latency` (non-array truthy) is silently reported as "nobody asked" instead of refusing
samples.evidence: `coderabbitLatency(perItem)` treats anything failing `Array.isArray` as not-requested (line 621) and returns `reason: LATENCY_NOT_REQUESTED` — "no timing records were passed to this scorer". A caller that passes a single item object, a Map, or the whole `corpusRecords` result wrapped in an object therefore gets a declared gap that blames the flag rather than the caller, with no indication that data WAS supplied and dropped. Everywhere else in this file a caller error `refuse`s (e.g. `wallMsOf` lines 183/188, `sizeOf` line 239); this path fails silently in the direction that hides the mistake.

samples.summary: `latencyCensus(perItem)` is computed twice, leaving `triggers` and `census.triggers` as two independent objects for one fact
samples.evidence: Lines 655 and 659 each call `latencyCensus(perItem)`; the result's `triggers` and `census.triggers` are then distinct objects holding the same counts. Besides doing the O(n) walk twice, it is two places for one fact to be read from — exactly what the surrounding comments argue against — and they would drift the moment either call site gains a filter. One call bound to a local, with `triggers: census.triggers`, is equivalent and cannot disagree.

verdict.reason: The core mechanism is present exactly as described: coderabbitLatency sets requested:true for ANY array (cost-latency.mjs:621,651), n_items is lats.length (:632,652) so an empty or latency-less array gives n_items===0 and self_timed.n===0; the completeness check at :797 is `0 < 0` → false so no shortfall reason is recorded; and declaredGaps({latencyMeasured: latency.requested}) at :866 with `if (!latencyMeasured)` at :692 drops the coderabbit_latency_ms gap entirely. The result is a retired gap with no figure and no reason — the exact state the docblocks at :664-667 and :678-680 say the block exists to prevent, while renderCoderabbitLatency (:976-985) prints "n/a (n=0)". Two details in the reviewer's evidence are wrong but not fatal: renderReport can never print "declared gaps — none" because cost_per_real_finding is pushed unconditionally (:683-691), and on the CLI path corpusRecords always attaches a latencyOf object (adapters/coderabbit.mjs:1150, :990-1001) over the same corpus version used for corpusItemIds (cost-latency.mjs:1088,1093), so an empty latency list also empties corpusIds and forces "partial" via :819. That coupling is incidental, not a guard on the predicate: costLatencyOf/coderabbitLatency are exported library APIs, and the substantive harm (gap retired with zero measurements and no shortfall reason, plus a denominator silently shrunk by .filter(Boolean)) remains reachable. Real logic/invariant defect in the correctness lane, so it stays.
